conventions: The mount-Hor phrase Hor ha-har (vv 22, 23, 25, 27): the English preposition belongs to Hor, the noun the Hebrew phrase opens with, and not to the appositive the ASV fronts ahead of it. vv 23 and 27 write that preposition on Hor itself (be-Hor ha-har -> in mount Hor, 'el-Hor ha-har -> into mount Hor) and the ASV renders it before mount, which is what settles the supplied unto of vv 22 and 25 under rule 33; the English order is not evidence against the Hebrew's. har takes only mount, and its article is unrepresented in all four verses because the ASV writes no the for the phrase (rule 29). Contrast v 28's rosh ha-har -> the top of the mount, where the ASV writes a the before each word and the article takes the one standing before its own.

In the double-accusative stripping and clothing clauses of vv 26 and 28, the marker on the first object is unrepresented and the marker on the second takes the preposition the English verb reaches it through — of in strip Aaron of his garments, upon in put them upon Eleazar — under rule 16's first family, the object noun keeping only its own English. The 'ot + suffix pair of vv 25 and 28 goes the ordinary way beside them: the suffix takes them and the marker has nothing.
report: Read all 58 candidate lemma groups, then all 29 verse dumps end to end for supplied English the lemma table is blind to. No cross-verse split found; patches is empty.

Multi-treatment buckets are licensed by the source or by what the ASV wrote: min as out of / from, be as in / with / through / by / on, the waw as and / or / so / Thus / wherefore / how / then. kol is attributive in vv 1, 14, 22 and 29 and the nomen rectum of 'ene in v 27, which is the only place the ASV writes an of for the relation, so rules 19 and 28 account for the difference rather than a split.

Hor ha-har (vv 22, 23, 25, 27) is uniform and is now recorded: the phrase's preposition goes to Hor, the noun the Hebrew phrase opens with, and the appositive's article is unrepresented in all four because the ASV writes no the. vv 23 and 27 write be- and 'el on Hor itself and the ASV renders each before mount, which is what settles the supplied unto of vv 22 and 25.

Supplied English is handled the same way throughout: the three appositional even units (vv 1, 22, 29) are all added under rule 16's limit, no marker standing on any of those phrases; supplied the, a, any and directional prepositions all join the nominal they determine (rules 15, 29, 33); supplied copulas, dummy subjects and subject pronouns join their predicates and verbs (rules 17, 20, 49). The only wholly supplied phrase, v 26's italic unto his people, is added, while the written 'el-'ammayw of v 24 is aligned beside it — the two sides of one formula, each treated correctly.

'ayin heads on the negation in both places: v 5 fuses the waw and 'ayin on neither is there, the existential frame joining the fused unit under rules 30 and 50; v 19 gives 'ayin the privative without. The v 5 note already names the competing split and why it was refused (it would leave a negative existential headed on any), so I let it stand.

BSB: 26 disagreements, none an error. 14 Td are articles the ASV writes no the for (the four demonstrative phrases and the mount-Hor appositives, rules 29, 41, 47); 7 R are the le of le'mor (rule 27), datives recast as bare English objects (rule 40) and the repeated la of v 15 (rule 22); 3 waws are v 3's, absorbed into lu's fixed Would that, and the apodosis waws of vv 16 and 29 that the ASV leaves unrendered; 2 object markers are ones whose suffix carries the English pronoun. No accepted edge was changed.

Considered amending rule 33 with the mount-Hor placement — that where the ASV fronts an appositive, a supplied preposition goes to the noun the Hebrew phrase opens with — and declined. The in-chapter proof from vv 23 and 27 is sound, but the packet shows no corpus precedent for har or Hor, and rule 33's 'the word it stands before' should not be qualified against precedent I cannot see. Flagged here for a chapter whose packet carries that lemma.

Minor, no patch: NUM.20.16's supplied in on qetseh is placed correctly but cited to rule 33; 'ir is Ncfsc, so rule 19's recast-construct-relation clause is the better citation. The edge is unchanged, and re-emitting the verse to fix a citation is not worth the risk.
